## `DelayedWork`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Threading.DelayedWork` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core` · mod API

Implements: `IDisposable`

A handle to one piece of main-thread work queued with a delay (`PostAfter` returns this instead of a bool). Dispose it, or call [`DelayedWork.Cancel`](#delayedwork--cancel), to drop the work if it has not started yet; once it runs, or after a cancel, disposing is harmless.

<a id="delayedwork--isaccepted"></a>

### `bool IsAccepted { get; }`

True when the dispatcher took the work; false when it refused it (see [`DelayedWork.RejectReason`](#delayedwork--rejectreason)).

<a id="delayedwork--ispending"></a>

### `bool IsPending { get; }`

True while the work is accepted and has neither started nor been cancelled.

<a id="delayedwork--rejectreason"></a>

### `MainThreadRejectReason? RejectReason { get; }`

Why the work was refused, or null when it was accepted.

<a id="delayedwork--cancel"></a>

### `bool Cancel()`

Drops the work if it has not started yet.

**Returns:** True when this call dropped it; false when it already ran, started, was cancelled or was never accepted.

<a id="delayedwork--dispose"></a>

### `void Dispose()`

Same as [`DelayedWork.Cancel`](#delayedwork--cancel); disposing twice is harmless.

<a id="mainthreadqueue"></a>

## `MainThreadQueue`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Threading.MainThreadQueue` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

The one main-thread dispatcher of the framework (it replaced twelve hand-rolled host queues). Any thread posts work; the Unity side calls [`MainThreadQueue.Pump`](#mainthreadqueue--pump) once a frame on the main thread. Pure: no Unity, a caller-supplied clock, so budgets, delays, timeouts and isolation are unit-tested.

- **Two lanes**. Work of a framework owner (any owner without the [`MainThreadQueue.ModOwnerPrefix`](#mainthreadqueue--modownerprefix)) runs first and in full every pump, as the per-feature pumps it replaced did, so a mod backlog can never hold back, say, Satone's restore. Work of mods (`mod:<id>`) runs after it, under the time budget, one item per mod in turn (round-robin), and at least one item per pump so a backlog always moves.
- **Order.** Within a lane (and within one mod), work runs in the order it became ready: posted work when it was posted, delayed work when it fell due. So a delayed item runs before anything posted after its due time, and after what was posted before it. Work posted while a pump runs waits for the next pump, so a job that re-posts itself cannot spin a frame forever. Tickers run every pump, after both lanes, regardless of the budget.
- **Isolation.** Nothing that runs here can throw out of [`MainThreadQueue.Pump`](#mainthreadqueue--pump): every exception goes to the failure callback (and, for an invocation, to the caller's task).
- **Timeouts are the caller's.** An invocation's timeout is a wall-clock timer on the caller's side, so a paused or stalled frame loop cannot hang the caller. Work that has not started when the timer fires is cancelled; work already running finishes and its result is discarded.
- **Owners.** Every item names its owner (a feature or a mod id). Queues are capped per owner as well as in total, so one runaway mod cannot starve the others, and [`MainThreadQueue.Cancel`](#mainthreadqueue--cancel) drops everything an owner still has waiting (mod shutdown).

### `void Invoke(string owner, string label, Action work, TimeSpan timeout)`

Runs work on the main thread and waits for it: inline when called on the main thread, otherwise queued and waited for up to `timeout`.

The work's own exception is rethrown to the caller.

**Parameters**

- `owner`: Who is asking.
- `label`: What the work is.
- `work`: The work.
- `timeout`: How long a background caller waits.

**Exceptions**

- `TimeoutException`: The main thread did not run it in time.
- [`MainThreadRejectedException`](#mainthreadrejectedexception): The dispatcher refused the work.
- `ArgumentNullException`: `work` is null.

<a id="mainthreadqueue--invoke-string-string-func-t-timespan"></a>

### `T Invoke<T>(string owner, string label, Func<T> work, TimeSpan timeout)`

Runs a function on the main thread and waits for it: inline when called on the main thread, otherwise queued and waited for up to `timeout`.

The work's own exception is rethrown to the caller.

**Type parameters**

- `T`: The result type.

**Parameters**

- `owner`: Who is asking.
- `label`: What the work is.
- `work`: The function.
- `timeout`: How long a background caller waits. Required: a blocked caller must always come back.

**Returns:** The function's result.

**Exceptions**

- `TimeoutException`: The main thread did not run it in time.
- [`MainThreadRejectedException`](#mainthreadrejectedexception): The dispatcher refused the work.
- `ArgumentNullException`: `work` is null.

<a id="mainthreadqueue--invokeasync-string-string-action-timespan-cancellationtoken"></a>

### `Task InvokeAsync(string owner, string label, Action work, TimeSpan? timeout = null, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)`

Runs work on the main thread and completes the task with its outcome.

**Parameters**

- `owner`: Who is asking.
- `label`: What the work is.
- `work`: The work.
- `timeout`: Wall-clock limit on the caller's side; null or `Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan` waits forever, and so does anything above `Int32.MaxValue` milliseconds (about 24.8 days, the timer's limit). When it passes, the task faults with `TimeoutException`.
- `cancellationToken`: Cancels the wait (and the work, if it has not started).

**Returns:** A task that completes when the work ran, faults with the work's exception (or a [`MainThreadRejectedException`](#mainthreadrejectedexception) when it was refused), or ends at the timeout or cancellation. Always queued, even on the main thread, so awaiting it from the main thread cannot deadlock.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentNullException`: `work` is null.
- `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`: `timeout` is negative and not infinite.

<a id="mainthreadqueue--invokeasync-string-string-func-t-timespan-cancellationtoken"></a>

### `Task<T> InvokeAsync<T>(string owner, string label, Func<T> work, TimeSpan? timeout = null, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)`

Runs a function on the main thread and completes the task with its result.

### `bool Post(string owner, string label, Action work)`

Queues work for the next pump, even when called on the main thread.

**Parameters**

- `owner`: Who is posting: a feature name or a mod id.
- `label`: What the work is, for failure lines.
- `work`: The work. Its exceptions go to the failure callback.

**Returns:** True when queued; false when the owner's or the total queue was full, or the queue is closed.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentNullException`: `work` is null.

<a id="mainthreadqueue--postafter"></a>

### `DelayedWork PostAfter(double seconds, string owner, string label, Action work)`

Queues work to run on the first pump at least `seconds` from now.

**Parameters**

- `seconds`: The delay on [`MainThreadQueue.Now`](#mainthreadqueue--now)'s clock. Zero, less or NaN is a plain [`MainThreadQueue.Post`](#mainthreadqueue--post).
- `owner`: Who is posting.
- `label`: What the work is.
- `work`: The work.

**Returns:** A handle: dispose it to cancel the work before it runs. When the dispatcher refused the work, [`DelayedWork.IsAccepted`](#delayedwork--isaccepted) is false and [`DelayedWork.RejectReason`](#delayedwork--rejectreason) says why.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentNullException`: `work` is null.

<a id="mainthreadqueue--pump"></a>

### `MainThreadPumpResult Pump(double budgetSeconds)`

One frame of work: moves due delayed items into their lane, runs every framework item that was waiting, then mod items round-robin until the budget is spent (at least one), then every ticker. Main thread only. Never throws.

**Parameters**

- `budgetSeconds`: Time allowed for the mod lane this frame, measured from the moment it starts. Framework work and tickers are not counted. Zero, less or NaN runs one mod item.

**Returns:** How many items ran and how many were left for the next pump.

<a id="mainthreadqueue--removetickers"></a>

### `int RemoveTickers(string owner)`

Removes every ticker one owner registered.

**Parameters**

- `owner`: The owner.

**Returns:** How many were removed.

<a id="mainthreadqueue--runorpost"></a>

### `bool RunOrPost(string owner, string label, Action work)`

Runs work now when called on the main thread (exceptions reported, never rethrown), otherwise queues it like [`MainThreadQueue.Post`](#mainthreadqueue--post). The call shape the Satone API has always had.

**Parameters**

- `owner`: Who is posting.
- `label`: What the work is.
- `work`: The work.

**Returns:** True when it ran or was queued; false when the queue was full or closed.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentNullException`: `work` is null.

## `MainThreadRejectedException`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Threading.MainThreadRejectedException` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Base: `InvalidOperationException`

The framework refused to run a piece of main-thread work. Thrown by the blocking `Invoke` calls and set as the fault of an `InvokeAsync` task. Derives from `InvalidOperationException`, which is what these refusals were before, so an existing `catch (InvalidOperationException)` still sees them.

**Parameters**

- `reason`: Why the work was refused.
- `owner`: Who posted it: a feature name or `mod:<id>`.
- `label`: What the work was.

## `MainThreadRejectReason`

enum · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Threading.MainThreadRejectReason` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core` · mod API

Why the main-thread dispatcher refused a piece of work.

| Name | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="mainthreadrejectreason--queuefull"></a>`QueueFull` | 0 | The owner's queue or the whole queue is at its cap ([`MainThreadQueue.DefaultCapacity`](#mainthreadqueue--defaultcapacity) and friends). |
| <a id="mainthreadrejectreason--ownernotrunning"></a>`OwnerNotRunning` | 1 | The owner is not running any more (a mod that failed or shut down). |
| <a id="mainthreadrejectreason--shuttingdown"></a>`ShuttingDown` | 2 | The game is quitting; the dispatcher accepts nothing new. |
